reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Regulating AI to protect rights and freedoms
themes.definition: AI and new technologies must be regulated democratically and aligned with human dignity, privacy, personal freedoms and democratic values.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling for regulation of AI in the name of rights, privacy, dignity or freedom of conscience and expression.
themes.exclusion: Calls for regulation framed around safety, military use or development without rights content.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for 'democratic regulation' of platforms and AI count here when tied to rights and dignity.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence and the data economy must, however, be better regulated and aligned with personal freedoms, respect for our private lives
Any technology must be used with one goal in mind — ensuring the dignity and rights of every individual.

themes.label: Disruptive technology cuts both ways
themes.definition: Recognition that AI and other disruptive technologies work for both good and bad, rejecting naive techno-optimism.
themes.inclusion: Passages stating that AI and related technologies are not automatically a force for good and can cut both ways.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements that technology outpaces human adaptation lean here when benefits are also acknowledged.

examples.quote: We forgot that all disruptive technologies work in both directions, good and bad.

themes.label: AI and platforms amplifying crises
themes.definition: AI grouped with social media platforms as amplifiers of disinformation, hate speech and existing crises.
themes.inclusion: Passages linking AI or platforms to disinformation or hate speech acting as accelerants of crises.
themes.exclusion: Passages that discuss social media without AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Where AI is only mentioned in a list with platforms, code here if the harm is information-related.

examples.quote: social media platforms, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies can act like steroids on our current crises

value.rationale: European passages treating AI as part of a broader set of emerging technologies that need rights-based regulation; Finland stresses dual use, Slovakia links AI with platform disinformation, and Belgium links AI regulation to privacy and freedoms.
